February 28, 1941.

Military Addairs Committee of the Nanking Government -
Recruiting Offices established in Shanghai.
----------
With reference to the remarks of the
Commissioner of Police on the attached translation
of an article, on the above subject, appearing in
the February 22nd issue of the "Tairiku Shimpo",
enquiries revealed that the Military Affairs
Committee of the Nanking Government has decided
to establish a "Central Military Training Regiment"
(中央陸軍士官教導團), with a view to strengthening
the basic army personnel. As a preliminary arrange-
ment towards achieving this end, the committee has
established a number of recruiting offices in such
leading cities and towns as Shanghai, Peiping,
Tientsin, Hankow, Hangchow and Soochow, etc.
The Recruiting Office in the Settlement in
Shanghai, which is designed as the 6th Recruiting
Area, is located at 427 East Seward Road, under the
charge of one Lieu Hat Tse (刘熙芝) who is
assisted by a Deputy named Ma Zu Ching (馬汝錦)
formerly a member of the Nanking Gendarmerie. Two
branches of the Shanghai Recruiting Office have been
established at 542 Chung Hwa Road, Nantao and at 93
Hsia Tang Ka, Sing Zang (新場), Pootung,
respectively.
Chinese youths between the ages of 18 and
25, with Senior Primary School and Middle School
qualifications, are eligible for enlistment at the
recruiting offices as cadets. The recruiting period
is between February 25 and April 15, 1941 inclusive

年龄在18至25岁之间、具备高小及中学学历的中国青年，均有资格在征兵办事处报名成为学员。征兵期为1941年2月25日至4月15日（含首尾两日）。

TAIRIKU SHIMPO :-
JAPANESE AUTHORITIES ADOPT STRICT PRECAUTIONARY MEASURES
AGAINST CHUNGKING TERRORISTS IN SHANGHAI

According to information from an
authoritative source, many Chungking terrorists have smuggled
themselves into Shanghai to carry out acts of terrorism in
the hope of restoring the Chungking regime's waning
influence in Shanghai.
It has been ascertained that Wong Choo-
ting (王佐廷), Wong Chao-kwei (王兆槐), Jen Min-san
(任明山), Lieu Chien-kuo (刘健民) and Hung Tang (洪同)
have been given a large sum of money with secret orders from
their leader Yang Hu (楊虎), formerly Woosung-Shanghai.
Defence Commander, to smuggle themselves into Shanghai and
to form an anti-Japanese terroristic organization. These
men seem to have already started their terroristic
activities in conjunction with Moo Chun (毛春), Tang
Shih-soo (湯是蘇) and others, who had been detailed to
Shanghai on a similar mission by Shang Kwei Yuin-siang
(上官雲相) of the Headquarters of the Third War Zone.
Besides the above-mentioned terrorists,
Tang Ts-liang (唐子良), a high staff-officer of the Third
War Zone, Tsoo Yen-han (左炎漢), a commander of the Kiangsu
and Anhwei Border Districts (苏皖边区指挥官) and others
smuggled themselves into Shanghai a few days ago under
secret instructions from Koo Tsoh-dong (顧祝同), Commander-
in-Chief of the Third War Zone.
It is also reported that a group of
some 40 terrorists have secretly arrived in Shanghai from
Hongkong or some other place.
In order to prevent acts of terrorism
by the Chungking elements, the Japanese authorities have
started secret investigations and have, at the same time,
adopted rigid precautionary measures.

Failure of Economic Plots of Chungking Terrorists
in Shanghai

We are informed that, owing to the
failure of its economic plans against Japan and the Nanking
Government, the Shanghai Branch of the National Economic
Reconstruction Committee (全国经济建设委员会) has been
ordered to close its headquarters in Chungking.

日本当局对上海重庆恐怖分子采取严格预防措施

据权威消息来源称，许多重庆恐怖分子已偷渡进入上海，企图实施恐怖活动，以期恢复重庆政权在上海日益衰落的影响力。
经查实，王佐廷（Wong Choo-ting）、王兆槐（Wong Chao-kwei）、任明山（Jen Min-san）、刘健民（Lieu Chien-kuo）和洪同（Hung Tang）已从他们的前吴淞-上海防卫司令杨虎（Yang Hu）那里获得巨额资金和秘密命令，偷渡进入上海并组建反日恐怖组织。这些人似乎已与毛春（Moo Chun）、汤是蘇（Tang Shih-soo）等人开始联合进行恐怖活动，后者是由第三战区司令部上官雲相（Shang Kwei Yuin-siang）派遣至上海执行类似任务的人员。

另有报道称，一群约40名的恐怖分子已从香港或其他地方秘密抵达上海。
为防止重庆方面人员实施恐怖活动，日本当局已开始秘密调查，并同时采取了严格的预防措施。

CONFIDENTIAL
February 21st 1941

"Kiangsu-Chekiang-Anhwei Pacification Army" of Nanking
Government renamed "1st Route Army"
----------

On February 15, 1941, the Kiangsu- Chekiang - Anhwei
Pacification Army ( 蘇浙皖綏靖軍總司令部 )
underwent a reorganisation and was renamed "1st Route
Army"( 第一方面軍總司令部 ). General Nyung Yuen-tao
( 任援道 ), with headquarters in Nanking, is still
the Commander-in-Chief.

The Kiangsu-Chekiang-Anhwei Pacification Army was
organized by the now defunct "Reformed Government" during
the latter part of 1939 and alloted eleven areas in the
Japanese occupied territories of Kiangsu, Chekiang,
and Anhwei Provinces. Each area was in charge of a
military officer ranking from "Major" to "Lieut-General."
The strength in each area varied from 500 men to 6,000
men. The total strength of this army was in the region
of 40,000.

In accordance with the reorganisation scheme, which,
it is expected, will be completed within one month: The
new "1st Route Army" will consist of 7 "Divisions," 2
"Independent Brigades" and 2 "Independent Regiments."
One division will consist of two brigades, each brigade
will consist of two regiments and each regiment will
consist of three battalions and each battalion will
consist of 500 men. In other words, a division will
have 12 battalions or a strength of approximately 6,000
men and the total strength of the 1st Route Army will
be in the neighbourhood of 50,000 to 60,000 men. A
list showing the disposition of the army is attached hereto.

南京政府“苏浙皖绥靖军”更名为“第一方面军”
----------

1941年2月15日，苏浙皖绥靖军总司令部进行了改组，并更名为“第一方面军总司令部”。总司令仍为任援道（Nyung Yuen-tao）将军，总部设在南京。

苏浙皖绥靖军由现已不存在的“维新政府”于1939年下半年组建，并在江苏、浙江和安徽三省的被占领土上划分了十一个防区。每个防区由一名军衔从“少校”到“中将”不等的军官负责。每个防区的兵力从500人到6,000人不等。这支军队的总兵力约为40,000人。

根据预计将在一个月内完成的改组方案：新的“第一方面军”将由7个“师”、2个“独立旅”和2个“独立团”组成。一个师由两个旅组成，每个旅由两个团组成，每个团由三个营组成，每个营由500人组成。换言之，一个师将有12个营，兵力约为6,000人，第一方面军的总兵力将在50,000至60,000人左右。随函附上显示军队部署情况的清单。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
02804
MAR 1 5 1939

“Reformed” Troops
Withdrawn
Guerilla Threat Reported
Successful Against New
Arrivals From Nanking

No Chinese “Reformed Government” troops were to be seen yesterday in the western district outside the defence perimeter, where they had been assisting the Japanese garrison in sentry and patrol duty for the previous two or three days. The village in which the new régime soldiers had been billeted also appeared to be empty, leading to the belief that these new troops had been withdrawn.
Chinese reports last night stated that the guerillas on Sunday night had inflicted serious losses on the new arrivals, who had not been properly equipped by the Japanese, apparently in fear lest they might turn against their sponsors. No official details of the losses suffered by the new régime forces could be obtained yesterday.

Retreat Towards Soochow
According to a Chinese evening report yesterday, at 5 p.m. on Monday the “Reformed Government” troops began retreating towards Soochow and Wusih. The report also stated that in view of the fact that the new Nanking troops are not well armed and that they have not been well disciplined, the Japanese and “Reformed” authorities had decided not to send more such troops to Shanghai.
Reports that there has been heavy fighting in the western district outside the perimeter have been circulated widely and they tended to strengthen the belief yesterday, that the newly arrived troops had been defeated. It could not be ascertained yesterday exactly how many of new “Reformed Government” troops had been sent to Shanghai, but it was learnt that they had come in large numbers.
They were first seen by villagers living in the district on Saturday last, when they were assigned to take up sentry duties in co-operation with Japanese soldiers at railway crossings. Guerillas there swore then that they would wipe out the new troops and since then fighting has been reported in progress.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》。
02804
1939年3月15日

“维新”部队
撤出
据报道游击队威胁
对新到的南京部队
取得成功

昨天，在防御 perimeter（防线/外围）以外的西区，看不到任何中国“维新政府”的部队，此前两三天他们一直在协助日本驻军执行哨兵和巡逻任务。这些新政權士兵曾驻扎的村庄也显得空无一人，使人相信这些新部队已经撤离。
昨晚中方消息称，周日晚上，游击队给新到的部队造成了严重损失，这些新部队因日本人担心他们可能倒戈反对支持者而未得到适当装备。昨天未能获得关于新政權部队遭受损失的任何官方细节。

向苏州撤退
据昨晚中方晚报报道，周一下午5点，“维新政府”部队开始向苏州和无锡撤退。报道还称，鉴于新到的南京部队武装不良且纪律不严，日本和“维新”当局已决定不再向上海派遣更多此类部队。
有关防线以外西区发生激烈战斗的消息广泛流传，这倾向于加强昨天人们认为新到部队已被击败的看法。昨天无法确切查明有多少新的“维新政府”部队被派往上海，但获悉他们是大批量进入的。
上周六，居住在该地区的村民首次看到他们，当时他们被指派在铁路道口与日本士兵合作执行哨兵任务。那里的游击队当时发誓要消灭这支部队，此后据报道战斗一直在进行。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
MAR 1 2 1939
62664

“Reformed” Troops
In Western Area
Assist Japanese Sentries
At Railway Crossings; Vow
Made by Guerillas

Numbers of Chinese troops belonging to the "Reformed Government" in Nanking have been drafted into the Western District outside the defence perimeter, it was learnt yesterday when they joined the Japanese army in sentry duty at the railway crossings and at important intersections and bridges in the Hungjao Road, MacLeod Road, and Rubicon Road areas. It was reported in Chinese circles last night that guerillas who have been active in those areas for the last few months have vowed to exterminate these new arrivals. Villagers from one of the cluster of houses near the Hungjao Road and the Golf Club had all evacuated last night.

Residents in the Hungjao area noticed the new Chinese troops for the first time when they appeared with the Japanese sentries at the railway crossings. The troops seemed to be of an inferior type and to be poorly equipped. They bore rifles but carried no ammunition belts. Further to the west, they had partially replaced the Japanese sentries. On bridges where formerly two Japanese were always to be seen were yesterday stationed two Chinese soldiers and only one Japanese. Police stations were being guarded by these Chinese.

A village off the Hungjao Road seems to have been taken over as the headquarters of these new arrivals, according to observers. Chinese troops were seen in numbers all over the village, but it proved impossible to make a guess as to how many were there.

Guerilla Attack

Some sharp burst of firing during yesterday afternoon caused a rumour to spread that guerillas had attacked the "Reformed Government" troops in that neighbourhood, but no confirmation could be obtained. It was learned from countryfolk, however, that the guerillas had declared that they intended to wipe out all these troops, which report caused a general exodus from villages and farms in the district. No firing had been heard in the neighbourhood up to a late hour last night, however, and nothing had occurred to lend any support to the rumours.

It will be recalled that a report that the "Reformed Government" had decided to send forces to Shanghai to assist in the so-called "silent war" to be waged on the foreign settlements a few weeks ago proved to be much exaggerated. Only between thirty and forty newly-trained policemen from the Nanking academy were being sent, it was stated. The arrival of these Chinese troops therefore caused considerable speculation yesterday.

《字林西报》。
1939年3月12日
62664

“维新”部队
在西区
协助日本哨兵
在铁路道口；游击队
发出誓言

据悉，南京“维新政府”所属的大量中国部队已被征调至防御 perimeter（防线/外围）以外的西区，昨日他们加入日军，在虹桥路、麦高包路（MacLeod Road）和鲁宾逊路（Rubicon Road）地区的铁路道口以及重要路口和桥梁执行哨兵任务。昨晚中方圈子报道称，过去几个月在这些地区活跃的游击队已发誓要消灭这些新来者。虹桥路和高尔夫俱乐部附近的一组房屋中的村民昨晚已全部撤离。

当新到的中国部队与日本哨兵一起出现在铁路道口时，虹桥地区的居民首次注意到了他们。这些部队似乎素质较差且装备简陋。他们携带步枪，但没有弹药带。在更西边，他们部分取代了日本哨兵。在以前总是能看到两名日本人的桥梁上，昨天驻扎的是两名中国士兵和一名日本人。警察局正由这些中国人守卫。

据观察者称，虹桥路外的一个村庄似乎已被接管作为这些新来者的总部。在整个村庄都能看到大量中国士兵，但无法猜测具体人数。

游击队袭击

昨天下午的一些激烈枪声导致谣言传播，称游击队袭击了该地区的“维新政府”部队，但未能得到证实。然而，从乡下人那里得知，游击队已宣布打算消灭所有这些部队，这一报告导致该地区村庄和农场的居民普遍外逃。然而，直到昨晚很晚时候，附近都没有听到枪声，也没有发生任何支持这些谣言的事情。

回想起来，几周前有关“维新政府”决定派遣部队到上海以协助对外国租界发动所谓“无声战争”的报道被证明是大大夸张了。据说当时只派遣了三十到四十名来自南京警校的新受训警察。因此，这些中国部队的到来昨天引起了相当大的猜测。

CHINA PRESS
MAR 1 2 1939

Japanese Plan
Puppet Army
Under Nanking

Plan Force Of 3,000,000
Soldiers At Fifty
Cents A Man

NEW 'TROOPS' TO
FIGHT GUERILLAS

Pootung Villages Said
Recaptured By
Partisans

Japanese plans to create a Chinese puppet army 3,000,000 strong at a cost of 50 cent's a man were revealed yesterday by the Tairiku Shimpo, Shanghai Nipponese newspaper.
The "army," according to the publication, will be composed of youths, and the movement will be launched though the "Reformed Government" of Nanking. The cost of the scheme, the newspaper declares, will be $1,500,000.
Although it is announced that the "army" will be devoted to the "establishment of peace and order in the three provinces and the development of a new China," with the suppression of the "red menace" as its immediate aim, it is reported from Chinese sources that an attempt will be made by the Japanese authorities to use their "recruits" against guerilla forces, which recently have become more active than ever and are causing the Japanese serious concern.
According to a translation from the Tairiku Shimpo, graduates of the "reformed institute," now in Japan, will form the nucleus of the "army," and after receiving special instruction, the youths will be returned to various points in the occupied territory for the purpose of organizing the proposed force.

Villages Retaken
Meanwhile, Chinese reports continue to give details of guerilla activities over a wide area.
Taking advantage of the incessant rainfall during the past few days, said the Wen Hui Pao yesterday, Chinese guerillas are reported to be making rapid strides in southern Pootung. Tinglin, strategic point in the southern part of Pootung, was attacked by the guerillas under Ting Hsi-shan and Wang King-san on Thursday. Japanese forces retreated to Nanchiao, the paper declares.
A severe clash is reported to have occurred in the vicinity of Nanchiao between the Japanese and the mobile units on March 8. Nanchiao is being sandwiched by the guerillas with the recapture of Siaotang, a nearby village.
Sintsang, another village in southern Pootung, has been the scene of guerilla warfare during the past two days. The Japanese are reported to have blown up all bridges leading to the village and constructed defense works in its environs.

《字林西报》
1939年3月12日

日本计划
傀儡军队
隶属南京

计划组建300万人的部队
每人成本五十美分

新“部队”将
用于清剿游击队

据称浦东村庄
已被游击队收复

上海日文报纸《大陆新报》昨日披露，日本计划以每人50美分的成本组建一支300万人的中国傀儡军队。
据该报刊载，这支“军队”将由青年组成，并通过南京“维新政府”发起这一运动。该报宣称，该计划的成本为150万美元。
虽然宣布这支“军队”将致力于“在三省建立和平与秩序并建设新中国”，且其直接目标是镇压“红色威胁”，但据中方消息来源报道，日本当局试图利用其“招募”的人员对抗游击队，这些游击队近期活动比以往更加活跃，令日军深感忧虑。
根据《大陆新报》的译文，目前在日本的“维新学院”毕业生将构成这支“军队”的核心，在接受特别指导后，这些青年将被派回占领区的各个地点，以组织拟议中的部队。

村庄被收复
与此同时，中文报告继续提供广泛地区游击队活动的细节。
据《文汇报》昨日称，利用过去几天的连绵阴雨，中国游击队在浦东南部迅速推进。周四，丁锡山和王金山率领的游击队袭击了浦东南部的战略要地亭林。该报称，日军撤退至南桥。
据报道，3月8日，日军与机动部队在南桥附近发生激烈冲突。随着附近村庄小塘的被收复，南桥正受到游击队的夹击。
浦东南部的另一个村庄新场在过去两天里一直是游击战的战场。据报道，日军炸毁了通往该村的所有桥梁，并在其周边构筑了防御工事。

报告称，周四，隶属于所谓“绥靖军”的一支150人傀儡部队分队在上海以西的沪闵公路上某处遭到伏击，残余的傀儡部队撤退至谢土坡（音译），并在那里得到了日军的增援。
据一位近日抵达此间的人士称，上海以西日占区的大量居民已逃入租界。据说，过去几个晚上，西部地区的枪声加剧。即使是那些已经习惯了炸弹和炮弹爆炸声以及机枪哒哒声的人，也发现居住在游击队出没、日军无力控制的地区是不安全的。
据悉，中国游击队实际上已控制了上海-无锡公路，在该公路上可以看到武装的中国哨兵。昆山镇正遭受持续的游击队袭击。

Subject (in full) Reported increase of Pacification Units of the Reformed
Government in Shanghai Area.
Made by D. S. Kamashita Forwarded by C Crawford

With reference to the attached translation from the
local Japanese newspapers regarding the reported increase of
pacification units of the Reformed Government in the area
surrounding Shanghai, I have to state that according to
reliable sources, the authorities of the Shanghai City Govern-
ment have planned to increase the pacification units in Shanghai
with a view to preventing the anti-Japanese and anti-new
regime activities from spreading to the area controlled by the
authorities. This suggestion was put to the Reformed
Government but so far no decision has been reached by the
Reformed Government.

March 4, 1939.
Morning Translation.

Sin Shun Pao (Japanese owned Chinese language newspaper):

UNITS OF PACIFICATION UNITS IN SHANGHAI

In connection with the concentration of
units of the Pacification Corps in Shanghai, the
Pacification Corps authorities have issued the following
statement:-
The "Reformed Government" has drawn up
certain measures to deal with the Foreign Settlements.
Crack units of the Corps have been concentrated in the
vicinity of Shanghai. The vanguard has already arrived
at a certain designated point and is in close touch
with the Japanese regular forces. The future activities
of the Corps will depend upon the attitude to be adopted
by the authorities of the Foreign Settlements.
The Pacification Corps will deal severely
with members of the Kuomintang and the Communist Party
who obstruct the administration of the "Reformed
Government".

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 5 MAR. 1939）

PACIFICATION AUTHORITIES TAKE SERIOUS VIEW OF
TERRORISM IN SHANGHAI

On March 2 the Pacification
authorities issued the following statement regarding
the concentration of a pacification detachment in
Shanghai:-

"In accordance with the policy of the
Government towards the Foreign Settlements important
bodies of troops are at present being concentrated at
Shanghai. The first troops have already arrived
at a certain place. The pacification troops are
maintaining close touch with the Japanese troops on
the spot. Future action by the troops will depend
upon the attitude of the S.M.C. The Pacification
Section will never pardon the activities of the
Kuomintang and communist elements who are obstructing
the administration of the 'Reformed Government' which
aims at saving the state and people, securing peace
and overthrowing communism."

Subject reported appointment of Defence Commissioner for the Shanghai

Made by. Det. Pan Lien-pih Forwarded by.

With reference to the attached translation of
an article on the above subject published in the
Standard dated February 13, 1939 and the Commissioner
of Police's remarks appended thereon, and the report
that the Pacification Department of the "Reformed
Government" in Nanking will despatch a batch of the
Pacification Corps to Shanghai, which appears in
the February 27th issue of the Hwa Mei Wan Pao,
exhaustive enquiries have thus far failed to obtain
any information that would confirm any of these
reports.

It is learned, however, that 200 cadets in
the Training Depot of the Police of the Shanghai
City Government at the end of February, 1939, were
converted into a unit to be known as the Military
Police Corps by the Japanese Military Special Service
Department. On March 1, 1939, these cadets were
each issued with a Mauser pistol without ammunition
but are still undergoing training. It is expected
that those recruits when their training is finished,
will be assigned for duty in the various localities
adjacent to the International Settlement and will
wear uniform similar to that of the Japanese troops.

PACIFICATION CORPS OF THE "REFORMED GOVERNMENT"
COMING TO SHANGHAI

According to news from a certain party,
the Pacification Department of the "Reformed Government"
in Nanking will despatch a batch of the Pacification Corps
to the Western District of Shanghai to help the Japanese
soldiers. As this may give rise to disputes over
territorial administration, Mayor Fu . of the Shanghai
City Government will probably refuse to approve the
measure. He expresses the opinion that the soldiers
of the Shanghai City Government in Pootung should be
used instead of the Pacification Corps from Nanking.
In order to frustrate the plan of Zung Yuan-dao (任援道),
Chief of the Pacification Department, 15 soldiers have
been sent to Shanghai with the approval of the Japanese
army in Pootung. If the situation requires, another
group will be despatched. They are mostly ex-bandits.

Guerrilla Activity in Western District

In view of the increasing activity of guerrillas in the Western District of Shanghai, the Japanese authorities have selected 320 men of the Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government, armed them and placed them on point duty in the vicinity of Zau Ka Tu and Poh Sing Kyung. However, as most of these policemen are drug addicts, they are in constant fear of attacks by guerrillas. They appear on the streets in daytime but after dusk they go into hiding in dark alleyways.

Activities of Female Guerrillas on Hungjao Road.

At 9 p.m. February 11, a Chinese Special Service Corps consisting of seven females, under the command of Wong Ching-san (王景山), had a fight with some 20 Japanese soldiers on Hungjao Road. Four Japanese soldiers were seriously wounded by pistol shots.

It is reported that some two days ago, several male and female members of this Special Service Corps led by Tung Ching-sung (董芹生) killed or wounded three puppet officials near Hungjao Road, while they also wrecked a police station of the Shanghai City Government.

A battalion of Chinese regular army, which arrived at Sz King (泗泾) and Tsipao (七宝) in the Western District of Shanghai the other day, is attacking Japanese soldiers. The Japanese have rushed reinforcements to the place. As a consequence, rice supplies and communications are interrupted. In Nantao there is no rice to be had.

西区的游击活动

鉴于上海西区游击队活动日益频繁，日本当局从上海特别市政府警察局挑选了320人，武装他们，并在曹家渡和波兴京（音译）附近部署定点执勤。然而，由于这些警察大多吸毒，他们时刻担心遭到游击队袭击。他们白天出现在街头，但黄昏后便躲藏在黑暗的小巷中。

虹桥路上的女游击队活动。

2月11日晚9时，由王景山指挥的一支由七名女性组成的中国特务队，在虹桥路与约20名日军发生战斗。四名日军被手枪击中，身受重伤。

据报道，大约两天前，由董芹生率领的这支特务队的几名男女成员，在虹桥路附近杀害或打伤了三名伪政权官员，同时还捣毁了一处上海特别市政府警察局。

日前抵达上海西区泗泾和七宝的一个中国正规军营，正在攻击日军。日军已向该地紧急增援。结果，大米供应和通讯中断。南市已无米可买。
